rows.grounds: reduplicated yathā expressing degree or proportion
fused compound tat + priya + kṛt; one who does what is pleasing to that
fused compound sarva + siddhi + īśvara; lord of all siddhis
optative of bhū in third person singular

items.question: How does the degree of pleasing that being relate to becoming lord of all siddhis?
premises: Pleasing that being increases siddhi lordship.
The practitioner becomes siddhi lord through pleasing acts.
items.inference: Greater pleasing action corresponds to greater attainment of lordship over all siddhis.
uncertainties: The referent of tat is supplied by surrounding context rather than this verse alone.
items.plain_english: The more one does what is pleasing to that being, the more one becomes lord of all siddhis.
